The full album was released on file-sharing sites and bootleg copies in 2004-2005 by an Elektra employee. Later on the album was brought to streaming platforms briefly in May 2022.

Name:
Original, Scrapped Version of Clipse - Hell Hath No Fury (2003-05)
(prod. The Neptunes)
Notes:
After releasing Lord Willin' and going on tour, Clipse began recording the album in late 2003. Work on the album was halted in 2004, when Arista Records. Their label at the time, was dissolved into its sister label Jive Records. As part of a larger merger between Sony Music Entertainment and BMG. Star Trak Entertainment moved on to Interscope Records, but due to contractual issues, the group was forced to stay with Jive. While Clipse resumed work on the album, its release was delayed by Jive throughout the rest of 2004 and much of 2005. Additional delays resulted when Clipse sued Jive after the label refused to grant the group a release from its contract. These legal issues would not be resolved until May 2006. Further delays pushed the release date to August 29 then to October 31 and then November 28. Two singles were released prior to the album. "Mr. Me Too" was released on May 23, 2006 and peaked at Number 65 on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart. The song contained a reference to their record label Jive where Pusha T apologized to the fans for the constant album delays and blamed them on the executives at Jive.
